items.t: Symptoms of seasonal allergic or perennial rhinitis in adults and children 3 years and over; nasal polyps in adults 18 years and over.

src.q: indicated for use in adults and children 3 years of age and older to treat the symptoms of seasonal allergic or perennial rhinitis
indicated for the treatment of nasal polyps in adults 18 years of age and older

restrictions.note: No prescribing restrictions stated in the UK nasal spray SmPC checked.

items.t: 2 sprays (50 micrograms each) in each nostril once daily (200 micrograms). Maintenance may be 1 spray each nostril (100 micrograms). If not controlled, up to 4 sprays each nostril once daily (400 micrograms); reduce once controlled.
items.tag: Allergic rhinitis, adults and children 12 years and over

src.q: The usual recommended dose is two actuations (50 micrograms/actuation) in each nostril once daily (total dose 200 micrograms).
the dose may be increased to a maximum daily dose of four actuations in each nostril once daily (total dose 400 micrograms)

items.t: 2 sprays in each nostril once daily (200 micrograms); if not controlled after 5-6 weeks, 2 sprays each nostril twice daily (400 micrograms). Re-evaluate if no improvement after 5-6 weeks of twice-daily use.

src.q: The usual recommended starting dose for polyposis is two actuations (50 micrograms/actuation) in each nostril once daily (total daily dose of 200 micrograms).
the dose may be increased to a daily dose of two sprays in each nostril twice daily (total daily dose of 400 micrograms)

items.t: Rhinitis, 3-11 years: 1 spray in each nostril once daily (100 micrograms). Not established under 3 years (rhinitis) or under 18 years (nasal polyps).

src.q: Children between the ages of 3 and 11 years: The usual recommended dose is one actuation (50 micrograms/actuation) in each nostril once daily (total dose 100 micrograms).
The safety and efficacy of NASONEX Nasal Spray in children under 3 years of age have not been established.
The safety and efficacy of NASONEX Nasal Spray in children and adolescents under 18 years of age have not been established.

items.t: Monitor height in children on prolonged treatment; if growth slows, reduce to the lowest effective dose and consider referral to a paediatric specialist.

src.q: It is recommended that the height of children receiving prolonged treatment with nasal corticosteroids is regularly monitored.

items.t: Hypersensitivity to mometasone furoate or any excipient.

src.q: Hypersensitivity to the active substance, mometasone furoate, or to any of the excipients listed in section 6.1.

items.t: Untreated localised infection of the nasal mucosa, such as herpes simplex.

src.q: NASONEX Nasal Spray should not be used in the presence of untreated localised infection involving the nasal mucosa, such as herpes simplex.

items.t: Recent nasal surgery or trauma, until healed.

src.q: patients who have experienced recent nasal surgery or trauma should not use a nasal corticosteroid until healing has occurred

items.t: Use with caution, if at all, in active or quiescent respiratory tuberculosis, or untreated fungal, bacterial or systemic viral infections. Warn about exposure to chickenpox or measles.

src.q: should be used with caution, if at all, in patients with active or quiescent tuberculous infections of the respiratory tract, or in untreated fungal, bacterial, or systemic viral infections
should be warned of the risk of exposure to certain infections (e.g., chickenpox, measles)

items.t: Not recommended with nasal septum perforation.

src.q: Nasonex is not recommended in case of nasal septum perforation

items.t: Systemic steroid effects are possible, mainly at high doses for long periods. Above-recommended doses can cause adrenal suppression: consider systemic steroid cover during stress or elective surgery. Moving from long-term systemic steroids needs care (adrenal insufficiency may last months).

src.q: Systemic effects of nasal corticosteroids may occur, particularly at high doses prescribed for prolonged periods.
Patients who are transferred from long-term administration of systemically active corticosteroids to NASONEX Nasal Spray require careful attention.

items.t: Raised intraocular pressure has been reported; refer to an ophthalmologist for blurred vision or other visual disturbance.

src.q: Following the use of intranasal corticosteroids, instances of increased intraocular pressure have been reported
the patient should be considered for referral to an ophthalmologist

items.t: Nasal polyps: one-sided, unusual, ulcerating or bleeding polyps need further evaluation.

src.q: Unilateral polyps that are unusual or irregular in appearance, especially if ulcerating or bleeding, should be further evaluated.

items.t: CYP3A inhibitors, including cobicistat-containing products, are expected to raise the risk of systemic steroid effects: avoid unless the benefit outweighs the risk, and if used monitor for systemic corticosteroid effects.

src.q: Co-treatment with CYP3A inhibitors, including cobicistat-containing products, is expected to increase the risk of systemic side-effects.
The combination should be avoided unless the benefit outweighs the increased risk of systemic corticosteroid side-effects

items.t: No interaction seen with loratadine.

src.q: A clinical interaction study was conducted with loratadine. No interactions were observed.

items.t: MHRA: corticosteroids metabolised by CYP3A, including intranasal, with ritonavir or cobicistat are not recommended unless benefit outweighs risk; consider beclometasone where possible.

src.q: there is potential for this interaction to occur even with non-systemically administered steroid formulations, including intranasal, inhaled, and intra-articular routes
use of beclomethasone should be considered where possible-particularly for long-term use

renal.note: No renal dose advice in the UK nasal spray SmPC checked.

items.t: SmPC: limited human data; animal studies showed reproductive toxicity. Should not be used in pregnancy unless the potential benefit justifies the risk. Observe infants of treated mothers for hypoadrenalism.

src.q: NASONEX Nasal Spray should not be used in pregnancy unless the potential benefit to the mother justifies any potential risk to the mother, foetus or infant.
Infants born of mothers who received corticosteroids during pregnancy should be observed carefully for hypoadrenalism.

items.t: SPS and BUMPS (allergic rhinitis in pregnancy): intranasal corticosteroids can be considered if non-drug measures are not enough; the dose reaching the baby is very small.

src.q: intranasal corticosteroids (for example, fluticasone) can be considered if non-pharmacological management is insufficient
The dose of medicine that reaches the baby in the womb is therefore very small and would not be expected to cause any adverse effects.

items.t: SmPC: excretion in milk unknown; decide whether to stop breastfeeding or the spray, weighing benefit to child and mother.

src.q: a decision must be made whether to discontinue breast-feeding or to discontinue/abstain from NASONEX Nasal Spray therapy

items.t: SPS: inhaled or intranasal mometasone can be used during breastfeeding; no specific infant monitoring usually needed.

src.q: When applied to the skin, inhaled or used intranasally, mometasone can be used during breastfeeding.
No specific infant monitoring is usually required.

items.t: No clinical fertility data; animal studies showed no effect on fertility.

src.q: There are no clinical data concerning the effect of mometasone furoate on fertility.

items.t: Nosebleed (very common with twice-daily polyp dosing), headache, pharyngitis, upper respiratory infection, nasal burning or irritation, nasal ulceration, throat irritation.

src.q: Epistaxis was generally self-limiting and mild in severity, and occurred at a higher incidence compared to placebo (5%)
Epistaxis Nasal burning Nasal irritation Nasal ulceration

src.q: systemic corticosteroid administration should be resumed and other modes of therapy and appropriate measures instituted

items.t: Examine the nasal mucosa periodically with use over several months.

src.q: patients using NASONEX Nasal Spray over several months or longer should be examined periodically for possible changes in the nasal mucosa

src.q: It is recommended that the height of children receiving prolonged treatment with nasal corticosteroids is regularly monitored.

items.t: Persistent nasopharyngeal irritation or local fungal infection may require stopping.

src.q: Persistence of nasopharyngeal irritation may be an indication for discontinuing NASONEX Nasal Spray.
If localised fungal infection of the nose or pharynx develops, discontinuance of NASONEX Nasal Spray therapy or appropriate treatment may be required.

items.t: Shake well. Prime with 10 sprays before first use; re-prime with 2 sprays if not used for 14 days or more. Discard after the labelled number of sprays or 2 months after opening.

src.q: Prior to administration of the first dose, shake container well and actuate the pump 10 times (until a uniform spray is obtained).
If the pump is not used for 14 days or longer, reprime the pump with 2 actuations
The bottle should be discarded after the labelled number of actuations or within 2 months of first use.

items.t: Use regularly; full benefit may take more than 48 hours. For seasonal rhinitis, start some days before the pollen season if symptoms are usually moderate to severe.
